description: Remove every remaining decimal hour rendering from the user-facing worklog payloads, so an hour quantity always reads as a clock duration ('32h 15min') and never as '32,25h'. The user reported this on the work item peek view after the previous change only converted part of the surfaces: the totals cards were converted, the equivalent-hours readings, the client-facing section, the allowance ledger and the dashboards were not, and the /preview endpoint sends no display twin at all so the form prints the raw '1.2500'. Independent of FEAT-003 (this one is API + payload wiring, that one is layout), but both must land before the change is reviewable as a whole.
steps: Read .kiro/steering/worklog-contexto.md rules R3 and R11 and docs/worklog/CONVENCOES-DE-TRABALHO.md first. R11 is a hard constraint: no change here may add logged_hours, raw_duration_minutes, applied_multiplier or any rate to a client-facing payload. The change is about how an hour is RENDERED, never about which hour a role receives.

In apps/api/plane/utils/service_log_time.py, make format_hours_human able to render a value that is not a whole number of minutes without falling back to decimal notation: append a seconds tail when a remainder exists, e.g. Decimal('1.8750') (112min 30s) -> '1h 52min 30s', Decimal('0.3750') -> '22min 30s'. Whole-minute values must keep their current output exactly ('1h 15min', '45min', '30h', '0min', negatives prefixed with '-'), because the existing assertions in apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_service_log_time.py::TestFormatHoursHuman all use whole-minute inputs and must keep passing unchanged. Round to the nearest whole second (ROUND_HALF_UP) as the last resort for a sub-second remainder, and document in the docstring why that is safe: logged hours are multiples of 0.25 and multipliers have two decimal places, so every real product is a multiple of 0.0025h = 9 seconds, and sums of such values are too.

Keep format_hours (decimal notation) in the module. Do not delete it: it is still the right renderer for spreadsheet output. State in its docstring that it is for exports and raw-number contexts, not for screens.

Switch these call sites from format_hours to format_hours_human: apps/api/plane/app/serializers/service_log.py get_equivalent_hours_display (around line 257, the technician's 'o cliente ve ...' reading) and the client row serializer's get_equivalent_hours_display (around line 404); apps/api/plane/utils/service_portal.py issue_client_totals (around line 510, both equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display); apps/api/plane/utils/service_allowance.py the ledger entry hours_display (around line 987); apps/api/plane/utils/service_pool.py the period snapshot displays (around lines 1791-1809, including the parcel hours_display); apps/api/plane/utils/service_reports.py (around lines 227 and 820, the aggregate *_display builders). In each case only the *_display twin changes; the raw decimal string field beside it stays exactly as it is, because the frontend types document that the raw value is what callers compare and sort by.

Leave apps/api/plane/utils/exporters/schemas/service_log.py on format_hours and add a one-line comment saying why: CSV/XLSX rows are read by spreadsheets and invoicing, where a decimal is the useful form. This is the one deliberate exception and it must be visible in the code.

Add the missing display twins to the /preview response in apps/api/plane/app/views/service_log/base.py (the `totals` dict built around lines 509-518): logged_hours_display, equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display via format_hours_human, alongside the existing raw strings and the admin-only amount fields. Then extend the `totals` shape of IServiceLogPreview in packages/types/src/service-log.ts with the three new readonly display fields.

Fix the frontend consumers of those values: in apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-form.tsx the split-preview total currently renders the raw string `preview.totals.logged_hours` ('1.2500') - render `preview.totals.logged_hours_display` instead; and in apps/web/core/store/issue/issue-details/service-log.store.ts change the EMPTY_TOTALS display seeds from '0h' to '0min' so an empty work item reads the same as one the server has answered for.

Grep the whole repo for any other place a raw hour string reaches the DOM (`grep -rn "totals\.\w*_hours[^_]" apps/web` and `grep -rn "_hours}" apps/web`) and fix any hit by switching it to the _display twin. Report what you found in findings even if the answer is nothing.

Update the tests that pin the old format: apps/api/plane/tests/contract/app/test_service_log_app.py lines around 735-736 and 753-754 assert equivalent_hours_display == '1,875h' - change the expectation to the new human string and keep the logged_hours_display assertion. Grep the whole test suite for other pinned decimal display strings (`grep -rn "h\"" apps/api/plane/tests | grep -i display` plus a search for the literal patterns '1,875h', '0,75h', ',25h') and update each. Do not weaken an assertion into a truthiness check: assert the exact new string, because a display test that only asserts 'something is there' is the false-green the conventions document forbids.

Add unit tests in apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_service_log_time.py for the new non-whole-minute behaviour: 1.8750 -> '1h 52min 30s', 0.3750 -> '22min 30s', a negative fractional value, and a value whose seconds are zero to prove no empty '0s' tail is emitted. Add a contract-level assertion that the /preview response carries logged_hours_display (in the existing preview test in test_service_log_app.py) and that the client work item totals no longer contain a comma-decimal hour string (assert the exact expected human string, not merely the absence of a comma).

Add an entry to docs/worklog/DECISOES.md as the next free decision number (D68 at the time of writing - check the file for the highest existing number) recording that every hour quantity on screen now reads as a clock duration, that format_hours survives for exports, that seconds appear only when the value is not whole-minute aligned, and that this refines R3's example ('1,25h quando o contexto exigir o numero') rather than contradicting the rule. Keep it in the same voice and structure as the surrounding decisions and in Portuguese, like the rest of that file.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "format_hours(" apps/api/plane returns hits only in apps/api/plane/utils/service_log_time.py (definition and docstring references), apps/api/plane/utils/exporters/schemas/service_log.py, and tests - no serializer, view, portal, allowance, pool or reports module still renders a decimal hour for a screen.
format_hours_human(Decimal('1.8750')) == '1h 52min 30s' and format_hours_human(Decimal('1.2500')) == '1h 15min', with every pre-existing TestFormatHoursHuman assertion still passing unmodified.

The /preview response contains logged_hours_display, equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display, IServiceLogPreview declares them, and the split-preview line in service-log-form.tsx renders the display twin instead of the raw decimal.
No client-facing payload gained a field: the client serializer and issue_client_totals still expose exactly the same field names as before the change (only their *_display values changed).
`./tools/agent-sandbox/run-api-tests.sh -m unit` and the three worklog contract test files pass, with no assertion softened to a truthiness check.
`ruff check apps/api` passes and `./tools/agent-sandbox/run-web-checks.sh types` passes.
docs/worklog/DECISOES.md carries the new decision entry.

review_response:
Answering the review at .agents/tasks/task-worklog-humanize-hours-and-responsive/2026-08-10-200538-review.md (verdict NEEDS_CHANGES, 10 issues). This field covers the API / hour-rendering half: issues 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9. Issues 4, 5, 6 and 10 are answered in FEAT-003.json.

ISSUE 1 - nothing is deployed. NOT FIXED, and not fixable from here. A sub-agent cannot push and cannot dispatch a workflow; the orchestrator's caller owns that. The diagnosis is accepted and unchanged: `git ls-remote --heads origin` still has no `fix/worklog-horas-legiveis-e-responsivo` and `git rev-list --count origin/preview..preview` is still 5, so the phone that reported '32,25h' is running a build that predates BOTH rounds of this work. What has to happen, in order: push `preview` (5 commits, including d5bd45b9f which introduced format_hours_human), push this branch, then dispatch `.github/workflows/build-branch.yml` by hand because it is `workflow_dispatch` only. Until that happens no screenshot from the phone can say anything about this code. Nothing in this commit changes that fact, and nothing in it depends on it.

ISSUE 2 - three failing consolidation tests. FIXED. `test_service_billing.py::TestTheConsolidation::{test_a_deviated_log_is_standalone_with_its_reason_beside_it, test_internal_work_is_excluded_from_revenue_not_listed_as_a_pendency, test_a_registration_pendency_carries_hours_but_no_amount}` now expect `hours_display` ('1h' in all three) inside the same EXACT dicts. Not loosened to subset checks, for the reason the review gives: `billing-tab.tsx` reaches that payload through `as unknown as` casts, so these assertions are the only structural guard the shape has. The registration-pendency test also gained an explicit `'amount' not in ...` assertion, so the absence that matters there is asserted rather than implied by dict equality.

ISSUE 3 - the verification ran a marker filter the conventions do not. FIXED, both halves. (a) The four unmarked files got the `unit` marker: `unit/utils/test_service_billing.py`, `unit/utils/test_service_money.py`, `unit/utils/test_service_pricing.py` and `unit/models/test_service_pricing_model.py` (the first, third and fourth had only `pytest.mark.django_db`, the second had nothing). Each carries a comment saying why the marker is there. `-m "unit or contract" --collect-only` now collects 2609 of 2611 tests, where the file that broke was invisible before. (b) Verification for this commit was run the way CONVENCOES-DE-TRABALHO.md prescribes: `./tools/agent-sandbox/run-api-tests.sh -q` with NO marker filter and no path filter -> 2611 passed in 558s.

ISSUE 7 - nothing guarded the single-renderer rule. FIXED. New helper module `apps/api/plane/tests/hour_display.py` (not a test module; pytest collects `test_*.py`) plus `apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_service_hour_display_contract.py`:
- `modules_rendering_hours_as_decimals()` walks every .py under `plane/app` and `plane/utils` and reports any module that imports or calls `format_hours`, excluding the two allowed files (`service_log_time.py`, which defines it, and `exporters/schemas/service_log.py`, the decided exception). The scan is AST-based, NOT a grep: six docstrings in this codebase discuss `format_hours` by name (two of them in `serializers/service_log.py` and `service_money.py`, which a regex version flagged on the first run), and a rule that fires on prose is a rule the next person deletes.
- A second test pins the allow-list to exactly those two paths AND asserts the export schema still binds `format_hours`, so if the export ever moves to the human renderer the exception shrinks with it instead of staying open forever.
- A third test proves the scan can actually fail: it detects an import, a bare call and an attribute call, and ignores a docstring, a comment and `format_hours_human`. A guard that cannot fail guards nothing.
- `hour_fields_missing_a_rendered_twin(payload)` is the twin invariant the review asked for: it walks nested dicts and lists and returns the dotted path of every `hours` / `*_hours` key with no `*_hours_display` sibling. Five self-tests cover the nested-list case, the bare `hours` key, the passing case and the not-an-hour case.

ISSUE 8 - new required type fields with no test. FIXED, all six plus two more:
- `overage_hours_display` on the CONTRACT-PERIOD preview: asserted in `test_service_billing.py::TestTheOveragePreviewSaysItIsIrreversible` ('3h') with the walker beside it.
- `overage_hours_display` on the ALLOWANCE preview: new `test_service_allowance.py::TestClosing::test_the_overage_preview_renders_the_hours_it_is_about_to_bill`. The case is deliberately NOT whole-minute-round: a 10h allowance against 25h15 of work gives '15.2500' -> '15h 15min'. Paired with a positive control (`test_a_surplus_has_no_overage_preview_at_all`) so 'no preview' cannot be confused with 'a preview reading zero'.
- `balance_hours_display` on both alert entries: asserted on the PANEL entries, which is where the twins actually live and what `attention-tab.tsx` reads -- period panel ('-3h') in `test_the_panel_groups_by_contract_and_counts_both_extremes` and allowance panel ('-15h') in `test_the_workspace_panel_lists_only_the_overrun_allowances`.
- `hours_display` on the consolidation: the three repaired exact dicts, plus a new `test_every_hour_in_the_consolidation_ships_a_rendered_twin` that builds a payload with an origin bucket, internal work and a non-round quantity (1h15) and asserts the walker finds nothing missing.
- `average_equivalent_hours_per_issue_display`: new `test_service_reports.py::TestD52AveragesArePresentationOnly::test_the_hours_average_ships_rendered_and_is_the_least_round_hour_in_the_feature`. 1.7222h is 6199.92 seconds, so it renders '1h 43min 20s' -- the clearest demonstration of why the seconds term exists. The absence case was strengthened too: an empty selection must carry neither the raw average nor the display, because a rendered '0min' would be an answer where there is none (D53).
- TWO FIELDS ADDED while doing this, and they are the only payload change in this commit: the period panel entry gained `granted_hours_display` / `consumed_hours_display` and the allowance panel entry gained `credited_hours_display` / `consumed_hours_display` (`service_pool_alerts.py`, plus the four fields on `TServicePeriodAlertEntry` / `TServiceAllowanceAlertEntry`). Without them the twin invariant did not hold for those two payloads and the walker could not be pointed at them at all. That is the trade: two rendered strings, and the entry is now structurally guarded so the next hour field added there cannot arrive bare.
- ONE DOCUMENTED EXCLUSION: `hour_fields_missing_a_rendered_twin(entry, skip_keys={'alerts'})` on the two panel entries. An alert's own dict carries the numbers that JUSTIFIED the code (`projected_hours`, `threshold_hours`, `discarded_hours`, `carried_hours`, ...) behind `TServiceAlert`'s `[detail: string]: unknown` index signature. No screen renders them -- `attention-tab.tsx` reads `alert.code` and `alert.severity` only -- and twinning ten diagnostic fields would grow every alert payload for no reader. The exclusion is named in the helper's docstring, in the tests that use it and in D68, and the day one of them is rendered it needs a `_display` like everything else. A self-test proves `skip_keys` does not excuse the level above it.

ISSUE 9 - `hours_display` on consolidation origins has no consumer. NOT DROPPED; kept, with the documentation corrected, which is the second option the review offered. Two reasons. (a) The invariant from issue 7 is exactly 'every hour key in a screen payload ships a rendered twin'. The origins bucket carries `hours`, so dropping its twin would mean the guard I was asked to add needs an exception list on its very first application, and 'the one bucket nobody renders yet' is how all four previous rounds of this defect began -- `/preview` shipped raw strings nobody was rendering yet either. (b) It costs one function call per bucket in a report an Admin loads by hand.
What WAS wrong is what D68 claimed about it, and that is fixed in docs/worklog/DECISOES.md: the literal-'h' defect was in the commercial pendencies, the registration pendencies and internal work. The origins table renders `amount_display` only. D68 now says exactly that, names the field as payload consistency rather than an observed defect, and says why the consistency is worth a field.
